lessons_used: Helpful changes: Reordering onboarding flow sequences, targeted functional hints (photo upload, path helper, sign-in security), select layouts (card carousel, single-click identity), key desktop flows (summon, visibility & control), and specific shortcut copy changes drove significant wins.

Harmful changes: Major structural redesigns (split personality), intrusive setup flows (desktop docking setup), spotlight path selector layouts, account persistence hints, and specific copy changes caused significant performance drops and early stops.
No clear effect: Wait, progress, and status indicators, background notifications, tutorial/showcase screens, and incentive badges consistently showed no clear effect.
Predictions too high: Large predicted gains (+8.0% and above) consistently overestimated actual performance, frequently resulting in smaller gains, no clear effect, or early test cutoffs.
Predictions too low: Major winning changes—especially shortcut copy, key desktop flows (visibility & control, summon flow), and story-first reordering—far exceeded low or negative predictions.

candidates.title: Desktop Interactivity Companion Flow
candidates.change: Add an interactive desktop widget preview sub-flow on the waiting screen where users practice summoning and placing their pet while graphics compile.
candidates.why: Home waiting stage has a massive mean time of 2336s, and support logs show users are confused about how to display or control the pet on their desktop after onboarding.

waiting.headline: Setting Up Your Desktop Pet
waiting.body: Try moving and interacting with your companion's desktop preview widget while we finish initial pet asset setup.

components.text: Click and drag to position your desktop pet anywhere on screen.

guard.reason: Enhances waiting screen with an interactive widget preview while continuing to inform that the pet is being prepared.

candidates.score_note: Key desktop summoning and control flows are strong drivers of success, though interactive UI has high cost.

candidates.title: Pet Style Crafting Redesign
candidates.change: Redesign the companion selection step into a streamlined visual card grid focus with direct style previews and quick mood badges.
candidates.why: Adoption stage is the biggest bottleneck in the funnel with only 64.2% conversion and a high median time of 89s.

guard.reason: replacement for 'pick_friend.pet_choices' does not do the job: needs 1 of ['choice_cards'] with real words

candidates.title: Post Companion Adoption Sign-In Sequence
candidates.change: Reorder the onboarding flow so user sign-in takes place after photo upload and adoption certificate creation, right before the waiting phase.
candidates.why: Moving account sign-in after pet customization builds ownership and intent, boosting overall funnel conversion from the low 32.9% baseline.

sign_in.headline: Save Your Pet to Account
sign_in.body: Sign in to securely link your newly adopted companion across all your devices.

guard.reason: Reorders sign-in to take place after adoption certificate while preserving all required onboarding steps.

candidates.score_note: Reordering sequences to build intent before sign-in aligns with historical wins and tested sign_in reorder gains.

candidates.title: Companion Persona Preview Screen
candidates.change: Insert a new introductory screen before path selection featuring short animated previews of different pet companion behaviors.
candidates.why: The choose_path step has an extremely high mean duration of 514s, indicating decision paralysis when choosing companion behavior paths without context.

new_persona_preview.headline: Discover Companion Behaviors
new_persona_preview.body: Each path brings unique desktop reactions, animations, and assistance styles.

guard.reason: Inserts a persona preview screen prior to path choice without removing any required onboarding steps.

candidates.score_note: Showcase and preview screens show no clear effect in past tests and carry high build cost.

candidates.title: Pet Photo Contrast Upload Hint
candidates.change: Display an actionable guidance hint on the photo upload screen explaining best lighting and background contrast for custom pet generation.
candidates.why: 3 support tickets reported custom pet generation failing or rendering visual artifacts during adoption.

upload_photos.hint: Tip: Use well-lit photos with simple backgrounds for optimal custom pet rendering accuracy.

candidates.title: Desktop Hotkey Control Launch Copy
candidates.change: Update the home completion screen headline and body to explicitly explain desktop hotkeys for showing, hiding, and speaking to the pet.
candidates.why: Support emails show post-onboarding confusion regarding how to summon, control, or hide the pet once on the desktop.

home_intro.headline: Your Companion is Ready on Your Desktop!
home_intro.body: Press Alt+Pet (or double click the system tray icon) anytime to summon, hide, or speak with your new pet.

guard.reason: Updates home intro copy to introduce desktop hotkey controls within onboarding.

candidates.score_note: Shortcut copy changes addressing desktop pet controls are proven winners and low cost.

candidates.title: Path Choice Carousel Layout
candidates.change: Switch the choose_path screen layout to a dynamic swipeable card carousel to highlight each path option clearly.
candidates.why: Choose path drop-off and high mean time (514s) show users need cleaner visual presentation to pick a path confidently.

guard.reason: Switches path choice screen layout to a carousel while retaining path selection functionality.

candidates.score_note: Card carousel layout changes are explicitly highlighted as successful layout improvements.

candidates.title: Account Restore Identity Security Hint
candidates.change: Add a prominent security hint on the sign-in screen informing users that signing in restores existing pets and prevents profile loss.
candidates.why: 8 support emails (the single largest complaint theme) were about missing or reset pets after signing back in.

sign_in.hint: Signing in ensures your desktop pet data is backed up and easily restored if reinstalled.

guard.reason: Adds account data backup guidance to the sign-in screen.

candidates.score_note: High support email volume points here, but account persistence hints are explicitly listed as harmful changes.

candidates.title: Desktop Background Setup Context Info
candidates.change: Update waiting screen text to provide clear technical context on background desktop engine initialization and asset compilation.
candidates.why: High mean waiting duration (2336s) leads users to think the desktop companion app has stalled or failed.

waiting.headline: Initializing Desktop Engine
waiting.body: We are preparing your companion's high-resolution desktop animations and background tray services.

guard.reason: Provides technical setup details on the waiting screen while retaining pet initialization messaging.

candidates.score_note: Wait, progress, and technical status context indicators consistently show no clear effect.

candidates.title: Adoption Certificate Action Confirmation Copy
candidates.change: Update adoption_certificate screen headline and primary button label to emphasize official companion binding.
candidates.why: Adoption is the funnel's lowest converting stage (64.2%), requiring clear, high-intent call-to-action copy.

guard.reason: Updates headline and button text on adoption certificate without removing required features.

candidates.score_note: Adoption step has the funnel's biggest drop-off (35.8%), giving high impact potential despite mixed copy test results.

Harmful changes: Major structural overhauls (split personality redesign, desktop docking setup), spotlight path layouts, account persistence hints, and specific copy changes caused severe performance drops and early test cutoffs.
No clear effect: Wait, progress, and status indicators, background notifications, tutorial or showcase screens, and incentive badges consistently showed no clear effect.
Predictions too high: High predicted gains (+8.0% or above) consistently overestimated actual impact, frequently yielding smaller gains, no clear effect, or early test cutoffs.
Predictions too low: Major winning changes—especially key desktop flows, shortcut copy, and story-first reordering—far exceeded low or negative predictions.
